system.name: Espresso
system.one_liner: constructs a cost-efficient CXL-based JBOF by sharing computing resources across SSDs

components.name: Espresso Host
components.role: host machine that issues NVMe I/O and runs the modified NVMe driver

components.name: NVMe Driver
components.role: host-side driver modified to redirect I/O commands and load-balance across SSDs

components.name: Espresso SSD
components.role: disaggregated SSD unit that can act as a Borrower or Lender of idle compute/DRAM resources

components.name: Compute-End
components.role: holds the SSD's processor and DRAM at moderate capacity; source/sink of harvested compute resources

components.name: Processor
components.role: onboard SSD processor, reserved at moderate strength to keep BOM cost low

components.name: DRAM
components.role: onboard SSD memory, reserved at moderate size to keep BOM cost low

components.name: Data-End
components.role: encloses flash resources and handles data transfer and flash I/O

components.name: DMA
components.role: engine that transfers data directly between host and flash backbone

components.name: Borrower
components.role: SSD short on compute resources that harvests idle resources from a lender

components.name: Lender
components.role: idle SSD that announces and lends spare compute/DRAM resources

components.name: Global Coherent Memory Space
components.role: CXL-exposed DRAM shared coherently across all SSDs, enabling inter-SSD communication

components.name: Lendable DRAM
components.role: the portion of each SSD's DRAM exposed as lendable via CXL

components.name: Idle Resource Descriptor
components.role: records which compute/DRAM resources an SSD currently has idle for harvesting

flows.what: exposes onboard DRAM via CXL to form a global coherent memory space
writes idle resource descriptors announcing lendable processor and DRAM
searches other SSDs' idle resource descriptors and chooses a lender
redirects portions of NVMe I/O commands originally targeting the borrower to the lender
lender's idle processor helps serve I/O commands by operating the borrower's metadata
lender sends DMA and flash operations to the borrower's DMA engine and flash controller
borrower transfers data directly between host and its own flash backbone, bypassing the lender
borrower caches part of its mapping table in the lender's DRAM (DRAM harvesting)

content.key_idea: Idle SSDs (lenders) advertise spare processor and DRAM over a CXL-shared coherent memory space so busy SSDs (borrowers) can harvest that compute/memory for I/O bursts, redirected transparently by a modified host NVMe driver.
content.reading_order: Top-down: Espresso Host and its NVMe driver first, then the row of Espresso SSDs (Borrower/Lender) with numbered arrows, ending at the shared memory space at the bottom.

palette.used_for: fill of the numbered circular step badges (1-8)
light gray fill for background panels (Idle Resource Descriptor, Lendable DRAM)

evidence: Figure 5 illustrates the overview of Espresso.
each SSD exposes portions of its onboard DRAM via CXL interconnections
the host NVMe driver redirects portions of NVMe I/O commands

summary: Espresso is a cost-efficient CXL-based JBOF that lets SSDs share onboard compute and DRAM instead of over-provisioning each drive. Figure 5 gives the system overview: an Espresso Host runs a lightly modified NVMe driver that redirects I/O and load-balances across a row of Espresso SSDs, each split into a Compute-End (a moderate processor and DRAM) and a Data-End (DMA engine and flash). All SSDs expose part of their DRAM into a Global Coherent Memory Space over CXL. A numbered 1-8 sequence traces the protocol: SSDs register lendable DRAM, an idle SSD (Lender) advertises spare resources via an Idle Resource Descriptor, a busy SSD (Borrower) picks a lender and has its I/O and metadata operations serviced remotely while data still moves directly between host and its own flash. A four-color legend distinguishes Control, Command/Operation, Data and Metadata messages.
